Remember this distinction: these representatives determine how products are sold to the appropriate business contacts, while technical salespeople determine how to sell complex solutions. One emphasizes relationships and price; the other expertise.

This career does not suit people who fear rejection, cannot handle performance pressure, or lack numerical understanding. Salespeople often carry quotas, attend business dinners, and worry about collections, which can be emotionally demanding.

A common path is: associate or bachelor's degree in business/marketing -> Sales Assistant at a factory or trading company -> follow customer orders -> independently manage a territory -> Sales Manager.
This career suits outgoing, resilient people who understand finances and cultivate trust. If you judge your work by whether goods become orders, you can thrive in this field.

Sales Representatives, Wholesale and Manufacturing, Except Technical and Scientific Products sell everyday, industrial, and consumer goods to business customers. They develop and maintain accounts, quote and negotiate, and follow delivery and collections, connecting factory capacity to market demand.

paragraphs: In the morning, review CRM to identify customers requiring follow-up and call to arrange visits. Meet buyers later in the morning to hear their needs, show samples, and present an offer. After lunch, calculate volume and rebates and adjust the contract template. In the afternoon, monitor factory delivery schedules and update customers. Before leaving, update the funnel and flag deals expected to close next week.
